H3PO2 (hypophosphorous acid) and H3PO3 (phosphorous acid) are good reducing agents because they contain P-H bonds. These P-H bonds can be oxidized to P-O bonds, allowing these compounds to act as reducing agents.

In H3PO4 (phosphoric acid), there are three P-OH groups and no P-H bonds.

Since H3PO4 has no P-H bonds (all hydrogens are attached to oxygen, not directly to phosphorus), it cannot be oxidized further in the same way and is therefore not a good reducing agent.

The correct answer is B: No, because the hydrogen atoms are not linked to the phosphorus.
